subproblem.title: A.e. finiteness of liminf of slice-mass majorants on all balls (V4(ii), step 7)
subproblem.statement: Assume (MM), the exact frozen third conjunct of the sibling theorem cbr_measure_convergence_tools: for all P ∈ ℕ, Borel measures μ_j on ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ), continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ, G ⊆ ℝ^P, a, b ∈ ℝ, L ∈ ℝ≥0 and Z_j : ℝ → [0, ∞] with μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}) < ∞ for all j and Z_j(t) ≤ L · liminf_{h↓0} ofReal(h⁻¹) μ_j(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for all j and t ∈ (a, b), there is a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] with liminf_j Z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for L¹-a.e. t ∈ (a, b) and ∫_{(a,b)} g dL¹ ≤ L · liminf_j μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}). Let P ∈ ℕ, μ_i (i ∈ ℕ) Borel measures on ℝ^P, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous, L ∈ ℝ≥0 and Z : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ → [0, ∞], (i, k, t) ↦ Z_{i,k}(t). Suppose that sup_i μ_i(B_{k+1}(0)) < ∞ for every k ∈ ℕ, and that Z_{i,k}(t) ≤ L · liminf_{h↓0} ofReal(h⁻¹) μ_i(B_{k+1}(0) ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for all i, k ∈ ℕ and all t ∈ ℝ. Then for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ, liminf_{i→∞} Z_{i,k}(t) < ∞ for every k ∈ ℕ.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (G : Set (Euclid P)) (a b : ℝ) (L : NNReal) (Z : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ≥0∞), Continuous f → (∀ j, μs j (G ∩ {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b}) < ∞) → (∀ (j : ℕ) (t : ℝ), t ∈ Ioo a b → Z j t ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μs j (G ∩ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t})) (𝓝[>] 0)) → ∃ g : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g ∧ (∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), t ∈ Ioo a b → liminf (fun j => Z j t) atTop ≤ g t) ∧ ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, g t ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun j => μs j (G ∩ {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b})) atTop) → ∀ (P : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal) (Z : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ → ℝ≥0∞), Continuous f → (∀ k : ℕ, ⨆ i, μs i (ball (0 : Euclid P) ((k : ℝ) + 1)) < ∞) → (∀ (i k : ℕ) (t : ℝ), Z i k t ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μs i (ball (0 : Euclid P) ((k : ℝ) + 1) ∩ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t})) (𝓝[>] 0)) → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ∀ k : ℕ, liminf (fun i => Z i k t) atTop < ∞
subproblem.natural_proof:
Write W_k := B_{k+1}(0) and Λ_k := sup_i μ_i(W_k), which is < ∞ by hypothesis.

1. Fix k, m ∈ ℕ. Apply (MM) with P, the measures μ_j, the continuous f, G := W_k, (a, b) := (−m, m), L and Z_j(t) := Z_{j,k}(t). Its hypotheses hold: μ_j(W_k ∩ {−m < f < m}) ≤ μ_j(W_k) ≤ Λ_k < ∞ (measure_mono, le_iSup); and the majorant inequality Z_{j,k}(t) ≤ L · liminf_{h↓0} ofReal(h⁻¹) μ_j(W_k ∩ {t − h < f < t}) holds for every t, in particular for t ∈ (−m, m). (MM) yields a measurable g = g_{k,m} : ℝ → [0, ∞] with (α) for L¹-a.e. t: t ∈ (−m, m) implies liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) ≤ g(t); and (β) ∫_{(−m,m)} g dL¹ ≤ L · liminf_j μ_j(W_k ∩ {−m < f < m}).

2. The right side of (β) is finite: every term μ_j(W_k ∩ {−m < f < m}) is ≤ Λ_k, so liminf_j μ_j(W_k ∩ {−m < f < m}) ≤ Λ_k < ∞ (Filter.liminf_le_of_frequently_le'), and L < ∞, so the product is < ∞ (ENNReal.mul_lt_top). Hence the lower integral of the measurable function g with respect to L¹ restricted to (−m, m) is finite, so g(t) < ∞ for a.e. t with respect to that restricted measure (MeasureTheory.ae_lt_top), i.e. (ae_restrict_iff' with measurableSet_Ioo) for L¹-a.e. t: t ∈ (−m, m) implies g(t) < ∞.

3. Combining (α) with step 2 (the intersection of two full-measure sets has full measure): for L¹-a.e. t, t ∈ (−m, m) implies liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) ≤ g(t) < ∞.

4. Fix k. A countable intersection of full-measure sets has full measure (ae_all_iff over m ∈ ℕ): for L¹-a.e. t, for every m ∈ ℕ, t ∈ (−m, m) implies liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞. For such t choose m ∈ ℕ with m > |t| (exists_nat_gt); then −m < t < m, so liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞. Thus for every k: for L¹-a.e. t, liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞.

5. Applying ae_all_iff once more, now over k ∈ ℕ: for L¹-a.e. t, liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞ for every k ∈ ℕ. ∎
proof_key_steps: For each k, m apply (MM) with G := B_{k+1}(0) and (a, b) := (−m, m); finiteness from sup_i μ_i(B_{k+1}(0)) < ∞.
The bound ∫_{(−m,m)} g ≤ L Λ_k < ∞ makes the measurable majorant g a.e. finite on (−m, m), so liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞ for a.e. t ∈ (−m, m).
Countable intersection over m (the intervals (−m, m) cover ℝ) and then over k gives the a.e. statement for all k.
